note: Block Access has no config entity, no settings form, no configure route (configure=null), no Drush and no plugins. Its only surface is permissions generated dynamically per block_content type by \Drupal\block_access\Permissions::get (permission_callbacks), plus a route subscriber that swaps block_content.add_form to the _block_content_access_create check (allow if 'administer blocks' OR 'create <type> block_content'). The active, non-deprecated permissions are 'update own <type> block_content' and 'delete own <type> block_content'; the create/update any/delete any variants are deprecated in 8.x-1.2 and removed in 2.0.0. Medium/hard cases are grounded in real user.role config and the dynamic per-type permission generation (the default 'basic' block content type exists on this site).

evals.prompt: On a Drupal 11 site with the contrib module block_access enabled, I want an editor role to be able to edit and delete only the content blocks (block_content) it created, WITHOUT giving it the site-wide 'Administer blocks' permission. Which permissions provided by block_access should I grant for the 'basic' block content type?
evals.expected_output: Grant 'update own basic block_content' and 'delete own basic block_content'. block_access generates these per block_content type via Permissions::get(); they scope editing/deleting to blocks the user authored, so you do not need 'administer blocks'.

evals.prompt: In block_access 8.x-1.2, which of its permissions are deprecated and what should I use instead? Name at least one deprecated permission and its core replacement.
evals.expected_output: The 'create <type> block_content', 'update any <type> block_content' and 'delete any <type> block_content' permissions are deprecated in 8.x-1.2 and removed in 2.0.0. Use core Block Content's own permissions instead: 'create <type> block content', 'edit any <type> block content', 'delete any <type> block content' (note 'block content' with a space, not 'block_content'). The 'update own' / 'delete own' permissions remain active.

evals.prompt: How does block_access change access to the 'Add content block' form (route block_content.add_form), and what determines whether a user may create a content block of a given type?
evals.expected_output: A route subscriber (block_access.route_subscriber) removes the default '_permission: administer blocks' requirement on block_content.add_form and replaces it with the custom access check '_block_content_access_create'. CreateBlockContentTypeCheck then allows access if the user has 'administer blocks' OR 'create <type> block_content' (checked with OR).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a user role with machine name 'ba_known_editor'. Inspect the live role configuration and state which block_access permission (for the 'basic' block content type) it has been granted.
evals.expected_output: The ba_known_editor role has the 'update own basic block_content' permission granted (visible in user.role.ba_known_editor config / via drush role:perm).

evals.prompt: This site has a block content type with machine name 'ba_promo'. block_access generates per-type permissions dynamically. Inspect the live permission list and give one of the OWN-scoped block_access permissions that exists for the ba_promo block content type.
evals.expected_output: Because Permissions::get() iterates over every block_content type, the ba_promo type yields 'update own ba_promo block_content' and 'delete own ba_promo block_content' (plus deprecated create/any variants). These appear in the permission list once the ba_promo block content type exists.

evals.prompt: This site has a user role 'ba_edit_role' that currently has no block permissions. Using block_access, grant that role the ability to edit ONLY the 'basic' content blocks its members authored (not all blocks, and no 'administer blocks'). Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Grant 'update own basic block_content' to the ba_edit_role role (e.g. drush role:perm:add ba_edit_role 'update own basic block_content', or add it to user.role.ba_edit_role permissions). The role must NOT be given 'administer blocks'.

evals.prompt: I have a role called 'ba_delete_role' on my site. I want people in that role to be able to delete the reusable content blocks they created themselves, but nothing else. Set that up using the block_access module's permissions for the 'basic' block type.
evals.expected_output: Grant 'delete own basic block_content' to the ba_delete_role role. The role must NOT receive 'administer blocks'.
